name: Cherry MX key switch, PCB mount (2 pins)
blurb: One mechanical keyboard key: a push switch that takes a standard MX keycap on its cross-shaped stem and connects its two pins while pressed.

pins.note: Seen from above with the LED window (the slot in the housing next to the stem) toward you, both pins are in the far half: pin 1 is right of centre, close to the far edge. The switch has no polarity; a keyboard matrix puts a diode in series with each key.
Left of centre and nearer the middle, seen from above with the LED window toward you. Pressing the key joins pin 1 and pin 2.

search: Cherry MX switch PCB mount 5 pin

verify: Keys sit on a 19.05 mm (0.75 inch) grid, centre to centre, both ways (Cherry: 19.05 standard, 16 mm minimum); the 14 mm body here is only the part under the plate, so place switches by the grid, not edge to edge. Body = lower housing, 14 x 14 mm and 5.0 mm from the PCB to the top of the plate: that is the plate cut-out, 14.0 +-0.05 mm square in a 1.5 +-0.1 mm plate (corner radius 0.3 max). The 15.6 x 15.6 mm flange rests on the plate; housing top is 11.6 mm above the PCB and the stem 3.6 mm more. The switch is pushed in from outside and clips into the plate, so a lid used as the plate must be 1.5 mm thick at the cut-out with the PCB 5.0 mm below its outer face; a printed lid thicker than 1.5 mm will not hold the clips (glue the switch or thin the lid around the hole). The case tool only knows 'stem just proud of the lid' and will seat the switch too low: set the height by hand. PCB holes, seen from above, relative to the centre: pin 1 at +2.54, -5.08; pin 2 at -3.81, -2.54 (1.5 mm holes); centre post 4.0 mm; PCB-mount (5-pin) switches also have two 1.7 mm plastic pegs at +-5.08, 0, which plate-mount (3-pin) ones lack. The Cherry layout and the KiCad footprint agree and both are drawn from the component side. Drawn for recognition only, scaled from the catalogue picture and not dimensioned there: flange thickness (1 mm), the upper housing as a straight box (it tapers to about 10.5 mm at the top) and the stem cross (about 4 mm across). Gateron, Kailh and other MX-compatible switches use the same holes and cut-out; low-profile types do not. Rating 12 V, 10 mA.
sources: https://cdn.sparkfun.com/datasheets/Components/Switches/MX%20Series.pdf (Cherry 'MX Series Keyswitch' catalogue pages 10-2 to 10-5, opened and read: 15.6 x 15.6, 11.6 housing height, 3.6 stem, 5.0 PCB to plate top, 3.30 pins; circuit board layout on a 0.05 inch grid with 4.0, 1.7 and 1.5 mm holes; metal frame cut-out 0.551 +-0.002 inch, frame 0.06 +-0.004 inch; 12 V 10 mA)

https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/product-files/4974/EN_CHERRY_MX_BLACK.pdf (Cherry MX1A-1xxx data sheet, opened and read: standard spacing 19.05 mm, 16 mm minimum, travel 4.0 mm, 12 V, 10 mA; no drawing)

https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints/-/raw/master/Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (KiCad footprint, opened: pad 1 at 0, 0 and pad 2 at -6.35, 2.54 with the centre hole at -2.54, 5.08, 1.5 mm drills, pegs 1.7 mm at +-5.08 from centre: the same pattern as the Cherry layout)
